rule: A difference that matches an entry is counted and listed in the report, never dropped. A run fails when an entry's count exceeds its bound. An entry with no cli_match cannot be reached by a CLI step through nginx; it is listed so later probe and failure-injection runs inherit it.

entries.summary: Node's math cache is shared with participationInit, reports and nextComment; polis-api's own cache sees only pca2 requests. Each serves the presentation it cached when it last filled, so the comment-derived fields (n-cmts, tids, pca.comment-extremity, which Node fills from the comments table when no math row backs them) can differ for one cache window. In the explicit within-window clock mode every cache window lasts the whole phase: after a moderation change or a new statement, Node can keep serving what a join or vote cached while polis-api serves what its first pca2 request cached.
nginx matches the normalised path (//pca2, %70ca2) but forwards the raw one; polis-api answers 502 and nginx asks Node. Only a client talking to polis-api directly sees the 502.
Trimming follows JavaScript's whitespace (U+FEFF counts, U+0085 does not), as Node's trim() and parseInt do. Listed because the generator's text classes include U+FEFF.
Database failures are 502s in polis-api, so nginx asks Node, which prints the Postgres error's fields in a 500 body; polis-api never prints database error text.
With NODE_ENV other than production, an unparseable JSON body gets Node's stack trace on Node and a plain message in polis-api. The stack runs with NODE_ENV=production.
A math_main.data value that is not a JSON object (no writer produces one) is answered 500 by polis-api.
Bodies over 1 MB, chunked, multipart, content-encoded or non-UTF-8 request bodies are refused, ignored or answered 502 by polis-api. nginx sends polis-api no request with a body.

harness_residuals_rule: Node or Postgres nondeterminism the fixture does not fix, found by the A/A control or by a database digest. A difference covered by an entry (a listed database column, or a listed CLI path of a listed command) is reported by entry and phase pair with its count, never dropped and never counted as a switch difference. Anything else, including a row-count difference, is not covered. An entry is removed when the harness pins its source.

harness_residuals.source: server/postgres/migrations/000000_initial.sql: users.site_id DEFAULT random_polis_site_id(), which draws Postgres random()
harness_residuals.effect: each user a sequence creates (every enrolled anonymous participant) has a different site_id in each phase
each conversation a sequence creates has a different zinvites.uuid in each phase

harness_residuals.source: server/src/invites/treevites.ts: invite acceptance and login-code use write now() in SQL, which the fixture clock does not reach (it pins Node's Date, now_as_millis() and the treevite column defaults)
harness_residuals.effect: wall-clock timestamps on used invites and login codes

harness_residuals.source: server/src/routes/comments.ts: the bulk statement route updates conversations.modified in a 100 ms setTimeout, conditionally (modified < value); server/src/routes/conversations.ts: the settings PUT sets it to now_as_millis(). conversation new sends its seeds and then its final settings PUT within one step, so the stored value is whichever write lands last; the barrier waits for both but cannot order them
harness_residuals.effect: a created conversation with seed comments stores one of two values for modified, depending on request timing; phase B's timing differs, so this can look like a switch difference
